rows.howToFix: Document consumption with a dealer oil-consumption test (measured top-offs over a set mileage) while the powertrain warranty is in force. Inspect the PCV system and turbo seals for oil ingestion, replace fouled spark plugs, and clean carboned intake valves (walnut blast) if buildup is found. Check the oil level frequently between changes and use the correct spec oil; severe consumption may require dealer powertrain repair under warranty.

rows.title: ABS Module Electrical Short Causing Engine-Bay Fire Risk (Recall 21V-161 / 007G)

Until repaired, park outdoors away from buildings. If the ABS warning light is on or the module has already been damaged, the hydraulic electronic control unit (HECU/ABS module) is inspected and replaced as needed.

rows.title: Electronic Parking Brake (EPB) Actuator Failure — Won't Release or Engage
rows.howToFix: Diagnose for EPB actuator/control-module fault codes and check for a stuck Auto Hold condition. Accepted fix is replacement of the rear EPB actuator (typically as part of the rear caliper assembly) followed by system calibration/clearing via a scan tool. Some owners have reset a stuck system temporarily by pulling the relevant fuses with the engine running, but replacement is the durable fix; some cases resolved under warranty goodwill.

rows.title: Front Brake Rotor Warping / Pulsation (Brembo Pad Deposit and Early Warping)
rows.howToFix: First try a proper bedding-in procedure (a series of firm high-speed stops) to even out and burn off pad deposits — this resolves the pulsation for many owners. If pulsation persists, measure rotor thickness variation/runout; machine or replace warped rotors and fit pads that run hotter/cleaner. Many owners upgrade to aftermarket slotted rotors and more aggressive pads. OEM front rotor for Brembo cars is 51712-J5500; DBA 4000-series slotted rotors are a common direct-fit upgrade.

rows.title: GDI Intake-Valve Carbon Buildup (Misfires, Rough Idle)
rows.howToFix: Definitive repair is mechanical intake-valve cleaning (walnut-blasting / media blasting) after removing the intake manifold — typically due around 40,000-80,000 miles depending on driving and oil use. Address any contributing oil consumption (PCV/valve guides) at the same time. A quality top-tier fuel, regular oil changes, and an occasional Italian tune-up slow accumulation; catch-can installation reduces future buildup. Replace fouled spark plugs and clear misfire codes after cleaning.
rows.dispositionReason: The solution prescribes an owner-buyable component or existing commerce requires re-review.

rows.title: Headlight Condensation and Moisture Causing Lighting Failure
rows.howToFix: Light fogging that clears after running the headlights a few minutes is considered normal. If you see water droplets/streaks or pooling, document it (photos over time) and pursue a warranty assembly replacement — dealers replace the full headlamp unit, which requires removing the front bumper cover. Minor recurring condensation can sometimes be managed by replacing the internal desiccant pack. Confirm you order the correct generation: pre-facelift (2019-2021) vs facelift (2022-2026) assemblies are not interchangeable.

rows.title: High-Pressure Fuel Pump Failure Causing Power Loss (Recall 24V-528 / 023G)

Dealers apply an updated ECM/engine-control software calibration and inspect the high-pressure fuel pump, replacing the pump assembly if it fails inspection. Out of warranty/recall, the OEM HPFP is replaced; the 3.3T uses Hyundai/Genesis pump 35320-3L000 and the 2.0T uses 35320-2CTB1. After replacement, clear codes and confirm fuel-rail pressure is within spec.

rows.title: Infotainment System Lag and Crashes
rows.howToFix: Update to the latest head unit software via the Genesis Connected Services app or dealer visit. The 2022+ models received significant hardware and software improvements. A factory reset can resolve persistent lag issues.

rows.title: Limited-Slip Differential Chatter Noise
rows.howToFix: Drain and refill the differential with Hyundai/Genesis-specified gear oil containing the correct friction modifier additive. The differential may need a break-in period after fluid change. This noise is somewhat normal for clutch-type LSDs.

rows.title: Parasitic Battery Drain / Dead 12V Battery
rows.howToFix: Load-test the battery and check charging-system output first; replace the AGM battery if it fails. If the battery is good, measure parasitic draw with a multimeter after the modules sleep (target under ~25-50 mA) and pull fuses to isolate the offending circuit — the head unit/infotainment is a common culprit. Apply any infotainment/BMS software updates, and have the dealer check for related service campaigns. A battery maintainer helps cars that sit for long periods.

If the mirror clicks and won't move, the actuator's internal fold gears are stripped — replace the fold motor/gear set or the mirror actuator assembly. Severe cases require the full mirror assembly.

rows.title: Soft Clear Coat — Easy Chipping, Peeling and Swirl Marks
rows.howToFix: For chips and stone damage, paint protection film (PPF) on the hood, fenders and mirrors is the most common preventive fix. For swirls, use proper two-bucket wash technique and a light machine polish followed by a ceramic coating to add a sacrificial layer. Document clear-coat bubbling/peeling early and pursue it under the paint warranty — some dealers have repainted affected panels for owners showing adhesion failure.

rows.title: Sunroof / Headliner Rattle and Creaking Noise

Owners have had partial success self-treating the sunroof foot with felt tape. Confirm whether any related sunroof-noise service bulletin applies to the VIN.

OEM left oil feed pipe/hose assembly is Hyundai PN 28240-3L100 (service kit references 28240-3L122QQH); inspect for oil weeping at the turbo and manifold, and address any oil-soaked heat shielding at the same time.

rows.howToFix: Dealers install a securing cap on the seat-belt pretensioners so that, even if a pretensioner over-deploys, the assembly is contained and cannot fling metal fragments into the occupant space. The remedy is performed free of charge; owner notification letters were mailed in May 2023.

rows.title: 12V Battery Drain When Parked

rows.title: OTA Software Update Failures
rows.howToFix: Ensure the vehicle is plugged in with a strong cellular signal during OTA updates. If an update fails, visit the dealer for a complete software reflash. Do not interrupt the update process by starting the vehicle.
rows.dispositionReason: The prescribed remedy is dealer, campaign, recall, or software work.

rows.title: Range Estimate Inconsistency
rows.howToFix: Precondition the battery and cabin while plugged in before departure. Use ECO mode and limit climate control usage in cold weather for maximum range. The BMS improves range predictions after learning driving patterns over several thousand miles.

On Electrified GV70s, confirm the ICCU recalls (025G / 24V-204 family) are completed, since ICCU failure is a major cause of repeat 12V deaths. Persistent draw with no obvious cause warrants module-by-module isolation by the dealer.

rows.title: Electrified GV70 Range Inconsistency
rows.howToFix: Precondition the battery while plugged in before cold weather departures. Use ECO mode for maximum range. The BMS learns driving patterns over time and range estimates improve after 2,000-3,000 miles of ownership.

rows.title: ICCU Failure Causing Loss of Drive Power (Electrified GV70)
rows.howToFix: Verify the VIN against the ICCU recalls (Genesis 025G; NHTSA 24V-204 and its expansions). Dealers inspect and replace the ICCU and its fuse as necessary and apply updated ICCU software, free of charge. If you experience warning lights plus a power-reduction message, pull over and arrange transport rather than continuing to drive. A repeat dead-12V battery on an Electrified GV70 should trigger an ICCU diagnosis, not just a battery swap.

rows.howToFix: Check the VIN against NHTSA recall 24V-205 (Genesis 020G). Until repaired, always set the emergency/parking brake and turn the ignition off when parked.

rows.title: Head-Up Display Fades / 'Eclipse' Effect Before Total Failure
rows.howToFix: Rule out polarized sunglasses (which kill HUD visibility) and direct sun overheating of the projector. If fade persists when cool, request HUD projector module replacement under 5yr/60k bumper-to-bumper warranty; out of warranty, full unit replacement runs ~$1100-$2200 installed.
